    (j : Fin (n + 1) ⊕ Fin (n + 1)) {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
findings.problem: This lemma rewrites a generated-lift point to the canonical numbered root matrix `rootSubgroupPoints …`. It has no simp attribute, although all five sibling versions of the same lemma are `@[simp↓]` with a `no_index` guard on the dependent lift term. Without the attribute, the type-B use in `Positive/BorelCandidate.lean` (line 140) has to instantiate the lemma by hand as `h` and then run a long `simpa only [BialgHom.mapDomain_apply, q, B, ofConv_toConv, AlgHom.id_comp, CommHopfAlgCat.hom_comp, BialgHom.comp_toAlgHom] using h`. The point also has to be rewritten into the lemma's shape first (`← generatedCoordinateMap_comp_generatedCoordinateLift`). The simp interface for this expression is therefore inconsistent across the generated-subgroup families.
findings.proposed_change: Mirror the sibling files. Put `@[simp↓]` on this lemma, with a comment that the rewrite must happen before `BialgHom.mapDomain_apply` unfolds the term. Wrap the dependent lift argument in `no_index`, i.e. `(no_index (toConv (q.ofConv.comp (generatedCoordinateLift n R (.inl j)).hom.toAlgHom)))`. The right side is the canonical form: the numbered root matrix, with no reverse rule. Then re-check `BorelCandidate` to see whether the manual `have h … simpa only` can become `simp` or `simpa`.
findings.benefit: The expression `pointToGeneralLinear (mapDomain … (generatedCoordinateLift … (.inl j)))` then normalizes to `rootSubgroupPoints …` in one step, as it does for E6, E7, D4 and type D. Users of the type-B generated subgroup no longer need to unfold `mapDomain` by hand. The simp sets stay uniform across families, so the same proof scripts transfer.
